extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: The first VQA dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case, sourced from online question answering community forums.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.inLanguage: en, es, fr, it, pt, zh, ko, eo, ru
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was scraped from the Stack Exchange archive, collecting examples containing a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors removed examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly-available data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For data format consistency, all images were converted to png format.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Removed visual questions with scores 0 or less, excluded visual questions with multiple images or visual answers, removed examples where the image could not be downloaded, and converted all images to png format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were recruited to annotate the user intent for 105 examples. They were provided instructions, taxonomy definitions, and examples, and asked to categorize the primary user intention. Two independent workers annotated each instance, and a third worker broke ties.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Two annotators tagged the category for each visual question, and disagreements were discussed and resolved. Agreement accuracy and Cohen's kappa agreement were calculated to measure improvement.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Located in the United States who had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating. Domain experts had at least a Master's degree in a related field.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Understanding user intent can help create human-centered VQA models for better user experience and provide answers that more directly meet users' needs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more data from countries like the US, India, and Europe, and less from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since the data is posted by users with access to mobile devices and the Internet.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of VQA models, including few-shot learning and zero-shot settings.

name.evidence: We introduce a new dataset called VQAonline.

description.evidence: We introduce the first VQA dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums, we call it VQAonline.

url.evidence: We publicly-share the dataset at: https://vqaonline.github.io/.

license.evidence: adhered to all data license restrictions (cc-by-sa 4.0) set forth by Stack Exchange.

creator.evidence: Chongyan Chen1, Mengchen Liu2, Noel Codella2, Yunsheng Li2, Lu Yuan2, and Danna Gurari1,3

inLanguage.evidence: The models work best on visual questions related to Germanic Languages; e.g., English... Romance Languages ( e.g., Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese), then East Asian Languages ( e.g., Chinese, Korean), and finally Pyccknn.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange... we collected all examples containing four components: a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. We used the publicly-available data...

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We removed visual questions with scores 0 or less for either the question or answer. Second, we excluded visual questions with multiple images ( e.g., GIF) or with visual answers... removing examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link... we converted all images to png format.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We then recruited crowdworkers to annotate the intent for 105 examples... We collected two user intention annotations from two independent workers (worker A and B) per VQA instance... we hired a third worker (worker C) to break the tie by instructing that individual to select one of the two provided user intentions.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We hired three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk to perform our task.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Two annotators (authors) tagged the category for each visual question. Any disagreements that arose were discussed and resolved... We observed slight agreement accuracy improvement and Cohen’s kappa agreement improvement after each round.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: For the final label, we used the majority vote label per VQA from 3 crowdsourced labels per visual question.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: we only accepted workers located in the United States who had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating... Each individual was a domain expert in one of ten topics... with at least a Master’s degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We utilized the state-of-the-art text spotter model DeepSolo to detect text for all images in our dataset.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: understanding and identifying user intent can potentially help create human-centered VQA models for better user experience. First, it facilitates the creation of datasets with better answers tailored to user needs.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Additionally, the geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: we highlight that this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Internet.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: VQAonline supports few-shot learning by containing training, validation, and test splits of 665, 285, and 63,746 examples respectively.
